A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReVisiT and share identifiable methods, experiments, and qualitative examples. All 30 pages of v2 and 31 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison despite the changed title and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, vision-token analyses, ablations, latency measurements, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds InternVL3-8B evaluations, further ablations, and detailed MMMU results.

M1.justification: The adaptive vocabulary constraint, minimum-JSD token selection, caching, and normalized probability-product refinement remain unchanged. v3 expresses v2 Equation (6) equivalently through log-probability addition and softmax. Its corrected Algorithm 1 resolves an inconsistency in v2's pseudocode rather than establishing a changed underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HallusionBench, CHAIR, POPE across the same three datasets and query types, VQAv2, and MMMU, and retain LLaVA-Bench-In-the-Wild qualitative examples. The additional backbone, subject-level reporting, and ablations do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparator set remains greedy decoding, DoLa, VCD, M3ID, CODE, and SID. v3 Table 14(c–d) adds evaluated comparison variants using KL or cosine selection and interpolation or weighted Product-of-Experts fusion, providing a limited expansion of design-choice comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds InternVL3-8B to the full benchmark evaluation and introduces additional ablation settings. Appendix D.1 revises VQAv2 scoring to the maximum score over whitespace-separated answer tokens and MMMU aggregation from item averaging to subject-macro averaging, dropping Win/Tie reporting. Appendix B.3 also changes GT/Hal probability normalization from the full vocabulary to the object subset. These are substantive reported protocol revisions; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained CHAIR subset, selection, layer, and threshold ablations, v3 adds JSD-versus-KL/cosine comparisons and interpolation-versus-weighted-fusion experiments in Table 14(c–d). Table 13 adds VQAv2 layer/threshold sensitivity for Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B. These substantially extend validation of the method's design choices.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same Wilson confidence intervals, paired Wilcoxon tests with Pratt handling and Holm adjustment, and fixed CHAIR sampling seed. Latency reporting retains six warmups, 300 samples, three decodings per sample, and mean plus standard deviation. The added latency series uses the existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive InternVL3-8B results, MMMU per-subject accuracies, and new ablation outcomes. The new backbone's ReVisiT/greedy scores include CHAIR F1 of 82.29/81.11 and VQAv2 accuracy of 68.40/68.73, showing mixed gains. Most retained headline scores and qualitative values are unchanged, but Qwen2.5-VL-7B SID F1 on POPE GQA-Random changes from 87.88 to 87.76. MMMU Win/Tie summaries are replaced by subject-level scores.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix C.2 introduces a KL-regularized variational objective and its closed-form Product-of-Experts solution, providing a limited theoretical justification for the existing refinement rule. Mathematical evaluation definitions also change, including best-token VQAv2 scoring, subject-macro MMMU accuracy, and object-subset probability normalization.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that vocabulary constraints expose interpretable vision-token semantics and that ReVisiT provides training-free, broadly applicable decoding with competitive five-benchmark performance and low overhead. The additional evaluations support the existing generalization claim without introducing a new core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of selection-metric and fusion-weight behavior and explains how unconstrained projections can reinforce repetitive generation. It explicitly limits empirical generalization to tested 7–32B open models, declining claims about substantially larger or proprietary models. The earlier limitations concerning visual overemphasis and unavailable external knowledge are retained.

D1.justification: v3 documents SID's approximately 10% visual-token selection for models with variable token counts, adds checkpoint/default-configuration guidance, and specifies alpha selection on a small validation split. It also documents InternVL3 settings and corrects the pseudocode. The code link, hardware, and latency measurement details are retained, although some disclosures move.

R1.justification: v3 more explicitly distinguishes using projected distributions to guide decoding from projection-based diagnosis, scalar confidence, and post-hoc verification, particularly in relation to Jiang et al. (2025a,b). The existing alignment taxonomy remains. NVLM and Wilcoxon references are removed; most cited research is retained.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title, extensively rewrites explanations, introduces a main-text Related Works section, and reorganizes the appendices into separate related-work, analysis, method, experimental-detail, and results sections. Limitations move before the references, and ethics, acknowledgments, and AI-assistance disclosures are added.

P2.justification: The paper changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures and tables. Figure 1 moves to the first page and gains a model; Figure 6 gains a third series and axis. Benchmark tables expand, new subject-level and ablation tables appear, and the final qualitative examples share a page.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens support for the decoding design through new selection/fusion ablations and fuller backbone evaluation, while correcting Algorithm 1 and explaining the refinement mathematically. These are useful gains over v2's already substantial evidence. Their benefit is limited by unexplained scoring-description revisions and inconsistencies in the new InternVL reporting: D.2 specifies last-layer selection, whereas the headline VQAv2 score matches Table 13's all-layer setting, and Figure 6 names different InternVL versions in its legend and caption.
